summary.title: Parsing Gigabytes of JSON per Second
summary.one_liner: Learn how the simdjson paper achieves gigabyte-per-second, standard-compliant JSON parsing on a single core by using SIMD instructions instead of conventional byte-by-byte parsing.
takeaways: JSON parsing can become a performance bottleneck because of data volume, and this paper targets making it as fast as possible.
simdjson is presented as the first standard-compliant JSON parser to process gigabytes of data per second on a single core on commodity processors.
It uses a quarter or fewer instructions than the reference parser RapidJSON, according to the abstract.
Unlike other validating parsers, it makes extensive use of SIMD instructions.
simdjson is open-source under a liberal license, so results can be reproduced.
summary.summary: This arXiv paper (Lemire and coauthors, first submitted in 2019 and revised through v7 in 2024) presents simdjson, a JSON parser that aims for standard compliance and gigabyte-per-second throughput on one CPU core. The abstract argues that substantial speedups are possible even though JSON parsing is a mature problem. It contrasts simdjson with other validating parsers by its heavy use of SIMD instructions, and reports using about a quarter or fewer instructions than RapidJSON. The page itself is only the abstract and metadata; the detailed method is in the linked PDF/HTML, which were not included in the page text provided.
